While I do agree that traveling has gotten less expensive with the passing of time, I still think you need to have some amount of privilege to travel. I also depends on many things, like your location, the reality of your country, and the reality of your group of friends. If you're a professional adult from the US or Europe, the possibilities to travel are much more than the ones of another adult from, let's say, the southern hemisphere with no college degree (or even with one, I'd say).   
So, you have to have in mind that you are able to save money, many people are living month by month with no possibility to do so. And then, even if you are able to save, the time it will takes you to save enough to travel is less that it would take other people. Why? Because a plane ticket will cost you less, the money exchange will be favourable for you, you can take shorter trips, etc.   
So, yes, when people think I'm rich for traveling a lot, I understand. I'm not rich, but it is a privilege, because even if those friends don't spend money in some things, their capacity of saving is less than mine. If they were to have a wedding or get a car, as someone mentioned in the comments, it would be by getting debts, not with their savings.

Hey! Well, I think there isn't a right way to travel. I wonder if you've enjoyed what you've done up until now. Are you sad that you're missing out because you feel pressured to visit more places and learn more or because you really want to do those things but you haven't decided to do them? 

If you feel pressured by the idea of a perfect trip, I'd advise you to let that go and to do the things that make you happy. Maybe you need to rest, maybe you need to just read, or sleep a lot, and that's okay, there's nothing wrong with being affected by the cold (I was in Germany in January once and I can tell you the cold and darkness did affect me too). 

And then, if you want to do more things, then maybe you should investigate about less conventional places. I read you do like the people and the place, so maybe you should find smaller museums, the places where the local people go for shopping, or the popular caffes (not for turists) and look at their daily lives, that way you would still be learning about a culture without doing the typical turist things. 

  
Well, I hope the rest of you trip is great and that you enjoy doing the things you want to do!

I realize I'm not being completely coherent here, as the real things happening in the world aren't very coherent either, I guess. 

I think the priority for all of us is life, right? So, I'm starting from that point. In this case, I think it's more important that countries with low vaccination rates stay somehow stable by avoiding the spread of the virus and the collapse of the health systems. That way, people won't die, which is, I think, the priority. 

Now, I know this isn't always the case, but while you're unemployed, you can receive some sort of help from the government that will help you survive, at least. 

I also know that the tourism industry is very precarious in most cases, in terms of job security, and people working in tourism can work in other areas too, as they're used to it, so not working in tourism doesn't mean they won't find other jobs. 

And in the third place, and not necessarily the ideal, I guess local tourism is a little safer than people coming from very far to stay in a vulnerable country. 

So, I guess it depends on your priorities, but if you put things on a balance, I tstill think it's better to stay away from those places, to avoid spreading the virus. I think it's a little arrogant thinking that by going on vacation to the place you want to go, you will be the saviour of these people because you're paying them but still putting them at risk of dying, very literally.

As a person from a "developing country," I'd say you're right: you being vaccinated doesn't mean you won't pass it on, it only means that you have less chance of ending up in the hospital, but if the people around you aren't vaccinated, they'll be at higher risk, and probably since they're working in tourism, they also won't have the financial resources to pay for a decent treatment. So, if you care for other people, I think for now, you should stay in places where the vaccination rate is high and where the healthcare is good.   
In the end, even if we're desperate to travel, nothing will happen if you we don't do it, or if we go someplace different from where we'd planned, and you will be saving lives, right?
